articles.title: Independence Day 2026: Know the unsung heroines of Bharat Mata; The tribal daughters who took down the British Empire
articles.description: On the solemn occasion of Independence Day (August 15), Bharat honours the fierce valour, unyielding patriotic spirit, and supreme sacrifices of its indigenous tribal communities-the unsung defenders of Bharat Mata. Long before the mainstream national discourse took shape, India’s tribal heroines stood as an indomitable wall of resistance, leading relentless crusades against oppressive foreign British rule to protect their Sanatan traditions, sacred ancestral lands, and civilisational heritage. Legendary tribal heroines like Rani Gaidinliu-the fearless freedom fighter from the North-East who waged a relentless holy struggle against British imperialism to safeguard her indigenous faith and culture – alongside Phulo-Jhano, Kanaklata Barua, and the young martyr Kalibai, injected immense spiritual energy, courage, and grassroots power into the Bharatiya freedom movement. Through armed resistance, social awakening, indigenous education, and deep self-sacrifice, these warrior queens and brave daughters of the soil shattered the shackles of colonial oppression, proving that the true heartbeat of India’s freedom struggle beat strongest in its native roots. This report brings to light the heroic sagas of these fierce tribal daughters of Bharat, whose unyielding courage, supreme sacrifice, and devotion to the motherland laid the bedrock of our civilisational resistance against foreign rule. Their timeless legacy stands as an immortal testament to the true, unsung guardians of India’s freedom and native heritage. Read More: India Supplies Refined oil to Russia: Symbolises global strategic energy footprint and bridges bilateral trade deficit Rani Gaidinliu: The Fearless Defender of Heraka Heritage and Naga Sovereignty Rani Gaidinliu (January 26, 1915 – February 17, 1993), hailed as the “Rani Laxmibai of Nagaland,” was a towering symbol of indigenous resistance from Tamenglong, Manipur. At the tender age of 13 in 1930, she plunged into the freedom struggle by joining forces with her brother Haipou Jadonang and Cousin in the spiritual and political Heraka Movement. The core objective of this sacred crusade was to banish colonial oppressors from their sacred soil, protect native cultural traditions against foreign encroachment, and re-establish sovereign Naga rule. Waging a relentless war against British imperialism, she became a beacon of civilisational pride for the North-East. Recognising her extraordinary devotion to the motherland, the Indian state conferred upon her the Padma Bhushan in 1982, issued a commemorative postage stamp in 1996 following her passing in 1993, and minted a special commemorative coin in 2015 to immortalise her glorious legacy. Ka Phan Nonglait: The Tactical Shield of Khasi Hills Ka Phan Nonglait (1799 – December 6, 1850) stands tall as the pioneering female freedom fighter of Meghalaya’s Khasi Hills, celebrated for her unmatched tactical genius and fierce resistance to British colonial expansion. Fighting under the heroic leadership of Khasi warrior U Tirot Sing, she executed one of the most brilliant guerrilla ambushes in indigenous military history. Spotting a battalion of British soldiers resting near a waterfall, she cleverly lulled them into a false sense of security by serving them refreshments. As soon as the invaders let down their guard, she swiftly disarmed them, casting their weapons deep into a rocky fissure within the stream and leaving them completely defenceless. This decisive act allowed U Tirot Sing’s forces to launch a crushing counterattack, annihilating 32 British troops and forcing a historic colonial retreat. Honored to this day through the landmark ‘Phan Nonglait Falls,’ her daring strategy remains a golden chapter in Bharat’s anti-colonial saga. Helen Lepcha: The Swadeshi Crusader of the Eastern Himalayas Helen Lepcha (January 14, 1902 – August 8, 1982), born in Sangmoo village, Sikkim, was a legendary tribal revolutionary who channeled the power of Swadeshi and self-reliance to dismantle colonial economic dominance. She travelled tirelessly across regions urging the masses to embrace native industries, spin the charkha, and awaken their innate love for Bharat Mata. Her selfless dedication shone brightest during the devastating 1920 Bihar floods in Muzaffarpur, where her relentless humanitarian relief work so deeply impressed Mahatma Gandhi that he affectionately named her ‘Savitri Devi.’ Continuing her fearless nationalist journey, she represented Sikkim at the 1921 Ahmedabad Congress Session alongside Dr. Sarojini Naidu, and later led a massive force of over 10,000 coal miners in Jharia to fiercely resist the exploitation of tribal labour. Honoured by the Bengal government as a Tribal Chief in 1958 and awarded the prestigious Tamra Patra alongside a freedom fighter pension by the Union Government in 1972, her life remains a powerful testament to native socio-political awakening. Sushila Samad: The Intellectual Pioneer and Munda Vanguard Sushila Samad (June 7, 1906 – December 10, 1960), hailing from the proud Munda tribal community of West Singhbhum, Jharkhand, shattered colonial socio-cultural barriers to become the nation’s first indigenous female ‘Vidushi’ (BA Honors graduate). Educated at Prayag Mahila Vidyapeeth, she seamlessly blended academic brilliance with revolutionary zeal, working as a Hindi poet, journalist, editor, publisher, and freedom fighter who mobilised tribal women toward political consciousness. When the historic Dandi March commenced in 1930, it was Sushila Samad who spearheaded the tribal women’s resistance movement across the Jharkhand region, proving that intellectual prowess and grassroots nationalism go hand in hand. Her trailblazing literary work and unyielding leadership during the independence movement laid a strong foundation for indigenous women’s empowerment and national pride. Tileswari Baruah: The Immortal Child Martyr of Dhekiajuli Tileswari Baruah (1930 – September 20 1942), a 12-year-old warrior girl from Dhekiajuli, Assam, etched her name in golden letters during the fiery 1942 Quit India Movement as a member of the elite ‘Mrityu Bahini’ (Suicide Squad). Bound by a sacred oath to unfurl the national tricolour over colonial police stations regardless of the ultimate cost, this young daughter of the soil marched fearlessly into the line of fire. On 20 September 1942, British bullets cut down her tender life, but her supreme sacrifice turned Dhekiajuli into a sacred shrine of Indian freedom. Celebrated annually as ‘Martyrs’ Day’ across Assam, her memory continues to inspire the nation; she was personally paid tribute by the Prime Minister during his visit to Dhekiajuli and honoured nationwide as a national child hero under the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign. Kanaklata Barua: The Immortal Flag-Bearer of Assam’s Freedom Struggle Kanaklata [...]

articles.title: ED attaches ₹37 crore assets linked to former AP minister in liquor transport probe
articles.description:
HYDERABAD: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has provisionally attached assets worth ₹37.7 crore linked to former Andhra Pradesh minister Karumuri Venkata Nageswara Rao, his son Karumuri Sunil Kumar, family members and others in the money-laundering probe into the Andhra Pradesh State Beverages Corporation Limited (APSBCL) liquor transportation case, as reported by TOI. The ED’s Hyderabad zonal [...]HYDERABAD: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has provisionally attached assets worth ₹37.7 crore linked to former Andhra Pradesh minister Karumuri Venkata Nageswara Rao, his son Karumuri Sunil Kumar, family members and others in the money-laundering probe into the Andhra Pradesh State Beverages Corporation Limited (APSBCL) liquor transportation case, as reported by TOI. The ED’s Hyderabad zonal office issued the attachment order on August 6 under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The agency said the assets represented direct proceeds of crime or assets equivalent in value to such proceeds.

Quarry rights, bank deposits and luxury vehicles also attached

The attached assets include prime land parcels in Kokapet and Khajaguda. The ED has also attached granite quarry lease rights over four hectares in Anakapalle district. Other properties include a commercial unit at Elan Paradise in Gurugram and a flat at Vasundhra Enclave in Delhi. Bank balances and fixed deposits have also been covered by the attachment order. Movable assets include a Volvo and a Toyota Fortuner, besides luxury watches purchased from Ethos Limited and Kamal Watch Company. The PMLA case stems from an FIR registered by the Andhra Pradesh Crime Investigation Department (CID) on February 10 based on a vigilance report.

ED alleges tender manipulation caused ₹195.32 crore loss

The case concerns the alleged centralisation of liquor transportation contracts by APSBCL. According to the ED, then APSBCL managing director Dontireddy Vasudeva Reddy, in alleged connivance with political leaders and private persons, replaced the district-wise transport system with a statewide contract without prior government approval. The agency has alleged that tender conditions were manipulated to favour pre-selected entities. Under the earlier system, transportation rates were around ₹19.6 per carton. The rates allegedly increased to ₹32-35 per carton under the new arrangement, while the work was subcontracted to local transporters for about ₹19-22 per carton. The ED has quantified the alleged proceeds of crime at ₹195.32 crore. Its June 2026 investigation update put the alleged loss to the government exchequer at about ₹195.33 crore. The agency has alleged that Kessireddy Raja Shekhar Reddy, former IT adviser to the Andhra Pradesh government, controlled front entities used in the alleged scheme. The ED has further alleged that Karumuri Venkata Nageswara Rao secured transport sub-contracts and demanded an 85% share of the profits, while Sunil Kumar managed operations through Sree Sudarsana Constructions. The alleged 85:15 arrangement and the role attributed to Sunil Kumar. The allegations are part of the ongoing investigation and do not by themselves establish guilt. ]]>

articles.title: 80th Independence Day : Unity in Diversity and Unwavering Faith in the Constitution Have Made India the World’s Largest Democracy says Anil Vij
articles.description: Haryana Energy, Transport and Labour Minister Sh. Anil Vij, extending greetings to the people of the state on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day, said that more than 1.4 billion Indians have established India as the world’s largest and strongest democracy through unity in diversity, democratic values and unwavering faith in the Constitution. He said this is a major achievement of the country’s eight-decade-long democratic journey. He added that the Haryana Government is continuously working to empower the four key pillars of Developed India identified by the Prime Minister—youth, farmers, women and the poor. Sh.Vij hoisted the national flag and took the salute at the district-level Independence Day program in Ambala. He extended Independence Day greetings to the people of Haryana and Ambala and also conveyed his best wishes to mothers, sisters and daughters on Hariyali Teej. He announced a holiday on Monday for the students who were scheduled to perform at the district-level programme and also announced a grant of ₹10 lakh to the district administration for the successful organisation of the event. Earlier, Sh. Vij paid floral tribute to the martyrs at the Shaheed Memorial in the Police Lines complex. He honoured war widows, families of freedom fighters, and distinguished individuals who participated in the Emergency and Hindi Movement. He paid homage to known and unknown freedom fighters who sacrificed their lives for India’s independence, as well as brave soldiers who attained martyrdom while defending the country’s borders. He said the government has accorded the highest priority to the honour and welfare of martyrs’ families. Over the past approximately 12 years, around 425 dependents of martyrs have been provided government jobs on compassionate grounds. 1857 Revolution and Shaheedi Memorial Sh. Vij said Haryana is a land of valour, sacrifice and patriotism. He said the spark of the freedom movement that emerged from Ambala on May 10, 1857, ignited the spirit of independence across the country. To preserve this glorious history for future generations, the construction of a grand Shaheedi Memorial in Ambala Cantonment is in its final stage. The memorial will serve as a permanent symbol of the sacrifice, struggle and patriotism of the brave freedom fighters. Developed Haryana Alongside Developed India Sh. Vij said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Sh. Narendra Modi, India is progressing rapidly towards self-reliance, innovation and economic growth. The government’s objective is to ensure development that reaches the last person in society. With this vision, the commitment to “Developed Haryana along with Developed India” is being taken forward. He said Haryana’s Gross State Domestic Product is estimated to reach approximately ₹15.18 lakh crore in 2026-27, representing growth of around 11 per cent over the previous year. The business environment for industries has been made simpler and more transparent, with processes for certificates, licences and approvals streamlined. The 2026-27 Budget places special emphasis on the revival of industrial areas and employment generation. The recently approved MSME Policy is expected to strengthen small industries and create employment opportunities at the local level. He said that on July 17, 2026, India’s first hydrogen train was flagged off from Jind Railway Station on the Jind-Sonipat route. Developed using indigenous technology, the train represents an important step towards demonstrating India’s technological capabilities and promoting clean and sustainable transportation. Poor, Farmers, Women and Youth Are Government’s Priorities Sh. Vij said the Haryana Government is continuously working to empower the four major pillars of Developed India—youth, farmers, women and the poor. As part of social justice measures, the income limit for the creamy layer among backward classes has been increased from ₹6 lakh to ₹8 lakh, while reservation has been provided to Backward Class-B in Panchayati Raj Institutions and urban local bodies. Under the Mukhyamantri Vivah Shagun Yojana, financial assistance of up to ₹71,000 is being provided for the marriage of daughters from poor families. Under the Mukhyamantri Awas Yojana, efforts are also being made to provide housing to poor families. In the health sector, eligible families are receiving free treatment up to ₹5 lakh under the Ayushman Bharat-Chirayu scheme. Free dialysis facilities are available for kidney patients in government hospitals and medical colleges. Low-income patients suffering from Stage III and Stage IV cancer are being provided financial assistance of ₹3,000 per month. Over the past 12 years, one medical university and 12 medical colleges have been established in the state. The number of MBBS seats has increased by 2,260, while 788 additional postgraduate seats have been added. For farmers, Haryana has become the first state in the country to arrange procurement of 24 crops at Minimum Support Price (MSP). These include wheat, mustard, sunflower, lentil, paddy, sorghum, millet, sugarcane, cotton and gram, among others. The Abiana system has been abolished, and steps have been taken to grant ownership rights to tenants occupying Shamlat land for 20 years. For women’s empowerment, ₹2,100 per month is being provided under the Lado Lakshmi Yojana. Women from poor families are being provided cooking gas cylinders at ₹500. The government’s objective is to make women not merely beneficiaries but active participants in the development process. Youth, Drug De-addiction and Sports Sh. Vij said that today’s youth will lead the construction of a Developed India by 2047. This year’s Independence Day theme, “Youth Power—Leading the Journey of Developed India 2047,” highlights the important role of young people. He also noted that the completion of 150 years of Vande Mataram is a matter of pride for the nation. Describing drug abuse as a serious threat to the youth and the future of society, he said “Drug-Free Youth, Healthy Families and Developed Haryana” is the government’s resolve. Under the nationwide drug de-addiction campaign, young people took a pledge at more than 28,000 locations across the country. In Haryana, more than 3,200 students, teachers and young people took the pledge for a drug-free India at a state-level programme at Kurukshetra University. Public awareness campaigns are also being conducted through programmes such as Raahgiri and Youth Marathons. Highlighting Haryana’s contribution to sports, he said the Indian contingent won 39 medals at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, with Haryana athletes making a significant contribution. Athletes from Haryana won 10 medals, including 7 gold medals, while the state’s daughters won five gold medals. Transparent and People-Centric Governance Sh. Vij said the government is committed to transparent, accountable and people-centric governance. Government services are being delivered to citizens at their doorstep through technology and online platforms. Along with providing jobs to youth on the basis of merit, the government is also focusing on skill development and training. He said that “The government belongs to the people, governance is for the people, and development can be achieved only through people’s participation.” He said that by 2047, when India celebrates the centenary of its independence, the responsibility of building a developed India and a developed Haryana rests with everyone. The vision is to build a Haryana where farmers are prosperous, young people become not only job seekers but also job creators, daughters are safe and self-reliant, industries receive opportunities, poor families live with dignity, villages and cities develop equally, environmental protection remains a priority, and public confidence in transparent governance continues to grow. Independence Day Celebrated with Great Enthusiasm Despite Rain Transport Minister Anil Vij hoisted the national flag and took the salute at the parade amid heavy rainfall. On the occasion, he said that despite the heavy rain, the 80th Independence Day was celebrated with great enthusiasm and dignity. Cultural programmes were scheduled as part of the district-level program, but could not be held due to the rain. He said the students had worked very hard and that these programmes would be organised and presented at another event. He announced a holiday on Monday for all students who were scheduled to perform at the district-level programme. He also announced a grant of ₹10 lakh to the district administration for the successful organisation of the district-level Independence Day program. District Police Contingent Secures First Place; GRP Ambala-1 Second and Home Guards Third At the district-level Independence Day program, the District Police contingent secured first place, the Government Railway Police (GRP) Ambala-1 contingent stood second, and the Home Guards contingent secured third place. Similarly, the Scouts and Guides contingent secured first place, Haryana Battalion-1 came second, and NCC Haryana Battalion-2 secured third place. Energy Minister Honours Officers, Employees, Journalists and Others for Outstanding Work Haryana Transport, Energy and Labour Minister Anil Vij honoured administrative officers, police personnel, students and sportspersons who had excelled in sports and education, as well as individuals who had performed commendably in various other fields, by presenting them with certificates of appreciation at the district-level Independence Day program. Those honoured included Gulshan Kumar, Stenographer; Sushila Kapoor; Yudhveer Singh; Sub-Inspector Ramesh Kumar; Sub-Inspector Narendra Kumar; Sub-Inspector Pradeep Kumar; Sub-Inspector Ravinder Kumar; Home Guard Mange Ram; Inspector Dharamveer; Anhad Kaur Antal; Vrinda; Komal Rani; Vikas Kumar; Kridha Gupta; Surinder Kumar, Clerk; PGT Vandana Rani; social worker Kiran Chhibber; Medical Officer Dr Amit Sharma; JBT teacher Shiv Kumar; Dr Cheshta Kashyap; Executive Engineer Ritesh Aggarwal; Executive Engineer Harbhajan Singh; Executive Engineer Devender Narwal; Executive Engineer Vikas Kumar; PMO Dr Pooja Paintal; social worker Jaswant Jain; Advocate Ajay Aggarwal; Bureau Chief Pawan Passi; journalists Devdatta Sharma, Tarun Kapoor, Ratan Singh Dhillon, D.N. Diwakar, Anil Dutta, Manjit Kaur, Parul Garg, Jaskaran Singh, Jitender Aggarwal, Niliki Sobti and Rahul; Editor Harender Gulati; and journalist Deepak Behal. Other dignitaries present on the occasion included former minister Aseem Goel Nannayola, Mayor Akshita Saini, Deputy Commissioner Sachin Gupta, Superintendent of Police Ajit Singh Sekhawat, BJP District President Mandeep Rana, Assembly Convenor Ritesh Goyal, SDM Darshan Kumar, City Magistrate Abhishek Garg, CEO of the Shivalik Board Pooja Kumari, Haryana Information Commission member Neeta Khera, State Spokesperson and Media Head Dr Sanjay Sharma, National President of Anti-Terrorist Front India Viresh Shandilya, former District President Jagmohan Lal Kumar, Anubhav Aggarwal, RTA Sushil Kumar, DIPRO Dharmendra Kumar, DDPO Dinesh Sharma, Municipal Council EO Devender Narwal, GM Roadways Ashwani Dogra, Civil Surgeon Dr Renu Beri, PMO Pooja Paintal, Executive Engineers Ritesh Aggarwal, Karnveer and Harbhajan Singh, Secretary of the District Sainik Board Colonel Sheoran, Advocate Sandeep Sachdeva, District Sports Officer Ram Swaroop, and BJP office-bearers Yatin Bansal, Vishal Rana, Gurvinder Singh Mankapur, Sanjeev Mishra, Beenu Garg, Harpal Singh Kamboj, Navinder Singh and Satish Sakya.

articles.title: I-Day Celebrations: Haryana Reaffirms Resolve to Build Viksit Bharat, Viksit Haryana by 2047
articles.description: Haryana celebrated the 80th Independence Day with patriotic fervour across the State, paying homage to freedom fighters, martyrs and the brave soldiers who continue to safeguard the nation. The State-level and district-level celebrations also provided an occasion to reaffirm Haryana’s commitment to the vision of Viksit Bharat and Viksit Haryana by 2047. The celebrations across the State reflected Haryana’s deep sense of patriotism and its commitment to the nation’s development journey. Vidhan Sabha Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Cabinet Ministers and Ministers of State unfurled the national flag at various programmes across the State, while recalling the sacrifices of freedom fighters and martyrs, and highlighted key initiatives being undertaken by the State Government to strengthen the welfare of every section of society and create new growth opportunities.They also called upon citizens, particularly the youth, to contribute actively towards building a stronger, self-reliant and prosperous Haryana in line with the national vision of Viksit Bharat. *India Building Global Economic Strength Alongside Its Cultural Heritage and Strategic Power-Vidhan Sabha Speaker Harvinder Kalyan* Haryana Vidhan Sabha Speaker, Sh. Harvinder Kalyan, addressing the 80th Independence Day function at Kurukshetra after hoisting the national flag, said India is strengthening its position globally through its rich cultural heritage, strategic strength and rapidly growing economy. Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, India is advancing towards self-reliance, innovation and economic growth and moving steadily towards the goal of Viksit Bharat. Harvinder Kalyan said development must go beyond economic growth and ensure benefits reach the poor, farmers, women, youth and every section of society. He said Haryana is working to strengthen the four pillars of Viksit Bharat—youth, farmers, women and the people at the last mile. He also stressed the need to protect the younger generation from drugs and highlighted the nationwide ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ campaign. Highlighting welfare measures, Krishan Kumar Bedi said the pension of freedom fighters and their dependents has been enhanced from Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 40,000, while around 425 dependents of martyrs have been provided government jobs during the past nearly 12 years. He also paid tribute to freedom fighters and martyrs, recalling their sacrifices in securing India’s freedom. Earlier, the Speaker paid floral tributes at the Shaheed Smarak and later inspected the parade and took the salute. He felicitated freedom fighters’ families, outstanding officials, employees and sportspersons, and announced Rs. 2.01 lakh for participating school students. *Diversity, Constitutional Values and Empowerment of Four Pillars Driving India’s Development-Energy Minister Anil Vij* Energy, Transport and Labour Minister, Sh. Anil Vij, addressing the Independence Day function at Ambala after hoisting the national flag and taking the salute of the parade, said India has emerged as the world’s largest democracy through unity in diversity, democratic values and faith in the Constitution. He said the Haryana Government is working to empower the four pillars of Viksit Bharat—youth, farmers, women and the poor—while ensuring inclusive development. He highlighted MSP procurement for 24 crops, the Lado Lakshmi scheme and healthcare benefits under Ayushman Bharat-Chirayu. The Cabinet Minister said Haryana is advancing towards Viksit Bharat with Viksit Haryana, with GSDP estimated at Rs. 15.18 lakh crore in 2026-27. He also highlighted the launch of the country’s first hydrogen train between Jind and Sonipat. Paying tribute to freedom fighters and soldiers, he said around 425 dependents of martyrs have been provided government jobs over the past 12 years. He also announced a holiday on Monday for participating students and Rs. 10 lakh for the district administration for the successful conduct of the celebrations. *Empowerment of Poor, Farmers, Women and Youth at Core of Haryana’s Development Agenda-Krishan Lal Panwar* Development and Panchayats, Mining and Geology Minister, Sh. Krishan Lal Panwar, addressing the Independence Day function at Panipat, said the Haryana Government is firmly advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat along with Viksit Haryana. He said development is meaningful only when its benefits reach the last person, with the empowerment of the poor, farmers, women and youth remaining a key priority of the government. He highlighted measures including free treatment for eligible families under Ayushman Bharat-Chirayu, MSP procurement for 24 crops, monthly assistance of Rs. 2,100 to women under the Lado Lakshmi Yojana, and Rs. 500 LPG cylinders for women from poor families. Calling for a collective resolve towards a drug-free youth, healthy families and Viksit Haryana, Sh. Krishan Lal Panwar said the government is undertaking extensive awareness initiatives against drug abuse, including programmes such as Rahgiri and Youth Marathons. He also highlighted the achievements of Haryana’s sportspersons, saying their performance at national and international platforms has brought pride to the State and serves as an inspiration for the younger generation. The Minister also emphasised the importance of employment and skill development opportunities for youth as part of Haryana’s development journey towards 2047. *Make in Haryana to Attract Rs. 55,000 Crore Investment, Generate 5 Lakh Jobs- Rao Narbir Singh* Industry and Commerce Minister, Sh. Rao Narbir Singh, addressing the Independence Day function at Sonipat, said Haryana’s economy is progressing rapidly, with the State’s GSDP projected at Rs. 15.18 lakh crore in 2026-27, reflecting an estimated 11 per cent growth over the previous year. He said the Make in Haryana Policy is expected to attract Rs. 55,000 crore investment in the MSME sector and create nearly five lakh employment opportunities by 2030. He also said six of the 10 proposed Integrated Manufacturing Townships (IMTs) have already been approved. Highlighting measures for soldiers and their families, the Minister said a Rs. 178.14-crore budget provision has been made for the Sainik and Para-Military Welfare Corporation, while 20 per cent reservation for Agniveers in government services has been provided under Haryana Agniveer Policy-2024. He also underlined the State’s focus on farmers, women and disadvantaged sections, including MSP procurement for 24 crops and monthly assistance of Rs. 2,100 to women under the Lado Lakshmi Yojana. *Education Reforms and Youth Empowerment Key to Viksit Haryana–Cabinet Minister Mahipal Dhanda* Education Minister, Sh. Mahipal Dhanda, while addressing the Independence Day function at Fatehabad after hoisting the national flag, said the State is committed to advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat and Viksit Haryana by 2047, with education, youth empowerment and inclusive development at the core of its priorities. Highlighting the transformation in school education, he said the number of Government Model Sanskriti Senior Secondary Schools has increased from 13 in 2014 to 218. He said the Super-100 programme is providing talented students from economically weaker and ordinary families with quality preparation and guidance for competitive examinations, while foreign language education has also been introduced in government schools, with French being taught in 37 schools and German language programmes also underway. He said the Government is simultaneously strengthening healthcare, farmers’ welfare, women’s empowerment and social justice. Under the Ayushman Bharat-Chirayu scheme, eligible families are receiving free treatment up to Rs. 5 lakh, while farmers are benefiting from MSP procurement for 24 crops. Emphasising the role of young people in building a Viksit Haryana, he said the Government is providing merit-based employment and skill development opportunities and is taking sustained measures to create a drug-free environment for the youth. He also called upon people to collectively contribute towards the goal of a drug-free youth, healthy families and a Viksit Haryana. *Tribute to Martyrs, Inclusive Development and Youth Empowerment at the Core of Haryana’s Growth-Cabinet Minister Vipul Goel* Revenue & Disaster Management, Urban Local Bodies and Civil Aviation Minister, Sh. Vipul Goel, addressing the Independence Day function at Faridabad, said the freedom enjoyed today was secured through the sacrifices of freedom fighters and brave soldiers, and carrying forward their ideals is a collective responsibility. He paid tributes to martyrs and their families and greeted the people of Haryana on Independence Day and Hariyali Teej. He said the festival of Hariyali Teej symbolises the State’s rich traditions of nature, culture and women’s empowerment. He noted that 425 dependents of martyrs have been provided government jobs on compassionate grounds during the past 12 years. He said Haryana’s economy is strengthening through balanced growth in agriculture, industry and services, with the State’s GSDP projected at around Rs. 15.18 lakh crore in 2026-27. He highlighted the first hydrogen train between Jind and Sonipat as a symbol of Haryana’s growing technological capability. He said the Government is working to empower the four pillars of Viksit Bharat—youth, farmers, women and the poor—through measures including Rs. 71,000 under the Chief Minister Vivah Shagun Yojana, Rs. 2,100 per month under the Lado Lakshmi scheme, Ayushman Bharat-Chirayu healthcare cover and MSP procurement for 24 crops. He said today’s youth will lead the journey towards a Viksit Bharat by 2047 and stressed the need for collective efforts against drug abuse. He highlighted Haryana’s achievements in sports and said the Government is strengthening sports infrastructure and facilities for young talent. He also said technology and digital platforms are enabling government services to reach citizens at their doorstep. During the function, he announced sports shoes for students participating in the Independence Day programme and a holiday for schools on Monday. *Take Resolve for Viksit Bharat-Viksit Haryana; Development Must Reach Every Section- Tourism Minister Dr. Arvind Sharma* Cooperation, Prisons, Elections, Heritage and Tourism Minister, Dr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, addressing the 80th Independence Day programme at Rohtak after hoisting the national flag, called upon citizens to take a resolve for building a Viksit Bharat and Viksit Haryana. He paid homage to the freedom fighters and martyrs whose supreme sacrifices secured the country’s freedom. Dr. Arvind Sharma said Haryana is progressing rapidly towards becoming a developed state under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with the Government focusing on the welfare of farmers, women, youth and poor families. Haryana is procuring 24 crops at MSP, while Lado Lakshmi Yojana provides Rs. 2,100 monthly assistance to women and Ayushman Bharat-Chirayu provides healthcare up to Rs. 5 lakh to eligible families. Merit-based government jobs and skill training are also being provided to youth. He said Haryana’s GSDP is estimated at around Rs. 15.18 lakh crore in 2026-27, registering nearly 11 per cent growth. The Government is promoting transparent and citizen-centric governance, while housing and marriage assistance schemes are supporting poor families. Highlighting healthcare and sports achievements, he said one medical university and 12 medical colleges have been established in Haryana over the past 12 years, adding 2,260 MBBS and 788 PG seats. Haryana sportspersons won 10 of India’s 39 medals at the recent Commonwealth Games, including seven gold medals. Dr. Arvind Sharma said around 425 dependents of martyrs have received government jobs on compassionate grounds over the past nearly 12 years. Recalling Haryana’s role in the 1857 freedom struggle, he said the Shaheedi Smarak at Ambala Cantonment is nearing completion and will inspire future generations. The Minister also stressed the resolve for a drug-free Haryana and urged youth to contribute to nation-building. He inspected the parade and took the salute of nine contingents, felicitated war widows and other achievers, while nearly 1,600 students from 16 schools presented mass physical exercises and students from eight schools staged patriotic cultural programmes. *Haryana Must Become a Developed State by 2047 with Prosperous Farmers' and Empowered Youth: Agriculture Minister Sh. Shyam Singh Rana* Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare Minister, Sh. Shyam Singh Rana, addressing the district-level Independence Day function at Sirsa after hoisting the national flag, said Haryana must contribute strongly to the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. He said the State’s goal is to ensure prosperous farmers, employment and entrepreneurship opportunities for youth, safety and empowerment of women, industrial growth, dignified living for every poor family, balanced rural-urban development, environmental protection and transparent governance. He said Haryana has a proud legacy of valour and sacrifice, recalling the role of Ambala in the 1857 freedom struggle. The Shaheedi Smarak being constructed at Ambala Cantonment is nearing completion and will preserve the legacy of the State’s freedom fighters. Shyam Singh Rana said the Government has accorded priority to the welfare of martyrs’ families, with around 425 dependents of martyrs provided government jobs on compassionate grounds over the past nearly 12 years.Highlighting farmer-centric initiatives, he said Haryana is the first state in the country to procure all 24 crops on MSP. He also highlighted the inclusion of 22 fruits and vegetables under the Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana. For Backward Classes, the creamy layer income limit has been increased from Rs. 6 lakh to Rs. 8 lakh, while reservation has been provided to BC-B in Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies. He said India is emerging as a global economic power and stressed that development must reach the last person. He urged citizens to work collectively towards building a Haryana that is prosperous, inclusive, environmentally conscious and developed by 2047. *Healthcare Expansion and Farmers’ Welfare Key to Inclusive Growth- Cabinet Minister Ranbir Gangwa* Public Health Engineering and Public Works Minister, Sh. Ranbir Gangwa, addressing the Independence Day function at Karnal, said Haryana is moving rapidly ahead in development, technology and the green economy. He said eligible families are receiving treatment of up to Rs. 5 lakh under the Ayushman Bharat-Chirayu scheme, while free dialysis facilities are available for kidney patients in government hospitals and medical colleges. He said the State has added 2,260 MBBS and 788 PG seats during the past 12 years. He said farmers remain central to Haryana’s development, with the State providing MSP procurement for 24 crops and abolishing the long-standing abiana system. He also highlighted Rs. 500 LPG cylinders for women from poor families and the Lado Lakshmi scheme. Referring to Karnal’s development, he said major projects including Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Medical University at Kutel, Maharana Pratap Horticulture University, the Outer Ring Road and elevated road project are progressing. *Present Generation Has Responsibility to Build a Strong and Prosperous India- Cabinet Minister Krishan Kumar Bedi* Social Justice and Empowerment Minister, Sh. Krishan Kumar Bedi, addressing the Independence Day function at Kaithal, said that taking India forward as a strong and prosperous nation is the responsibility of the present generation. He called for collective efforts to realise the vision of Viksit Bharat and Viksit Haryana by 2047, with the youth playing a decisive role in this journey. Highlighting welfare measures, Sh. Krishan Kumar Bedi said the pension of freedom fighters and their dependents has been enhanced from Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 40,000. In contrast, around 425 dependents of martyrs have been provided government jobs during the past nearly 12 years. Referring to Kaithal’s development, he said the Bhagwan Parshuram Medical College, being constructed at a cost of around Rs. 1,000 crore, is nearing completion and will be started soon. He also highlighted the district’s Nursing College and Maharishi Valmiki Sanskrit University. *Haryana Moving Rapidly Towards a Self-Reliant India by Empowering Farmers, Women and Youth-Cabinet Minister Shruti Choudhary* Women and Child Development Minister, Ms. Shruti Choudhary, addressing the 80th Independence Day function at Panchkula after hoisting the national flag, said Haryana is moving rapidly towards a self-reliant India and playing a key role in the country’s development journey. She said Haryana is a land of valour, sacrifice and patriotism and recalled the contribution of the State to the 1857 freedom struggle. Around 425 dependents of martyrs have been provided government jobs over the past nearly 12 years, reflecting the Government’s commitment to their families. Highlighting development initiatives, Ms. Shruti Choudhary said Haryana is the first state to procure 24 crops at MSP, while 22 fruits and vegetables are covered under the Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana. The State is also expanding healthcare facilities, including free dialysis, hepatitis testing and vaccination, and free single-donor platelets for dengue patients. She said projects worth Rs. 5,714 crore are being approved under the Jal Surakshit Haryana programme, including rehabilitation of 678 canals, 620 watercourses and 120 canal-based micro-irrigation projects. Another 131 water bodies will be developed for rainwater conservation and groundwater recharge, while nearly two lakh acres will be freed from waterlogging. Emphasising women’s empowerment, she said eligible women receive Rs. 2,100 per month under the Lado Lakshmi Yojana, while poor families are being provided LPG cylinders at Rs. 500. More than 4,000 playway schools have also been established under NEP-2020. Referring to this year’s theme, ‘Yuva Shakti—Leading the Journey of Viksit Bharat 2047’, Ms. Shruti Choudhary urged youth to stay away from drugs and contribute through education, skills, employment, sports and entrepreneurship. She highlighted Haryana athletes’ 10-medal haul, including seven gold medals, at the recent Commonwealth Games. *Women’s Empowerment Integral to India’s Journey Towards Becoming a Developed Nation-Health Minister Arti Singh Rao* Health and Ayush Minister, Ms Arti Singh Rao, addressing the Independence Day function at Jhajjar after hoisting the national flag, said India is moving steadily towards becoming a developed nation under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with women’s empowerment playing a key role in this journey. She said development is meaningful only when its benefits reach the last person, with the government focusing on the welfare and empowerment of the poor, farmers, women, youth and disadvantaged sections. She highlighted the State Government’s efforts to strengthen healthcare infrastructure, stating that Haryana has added one medical university and 12 medical colleges over the past 12 years, along with 2,260 MBBS and 788 postgraduate seats. She said free dialysis facilities are available for kidney patients at government hospitals and medical colleges, while financial assistance is being provided to eligible cancer patients. She also emphasised the need to empower youth through sports, education and skill development and urged young people to stay away from drugs and contribute to nation-building. Referring to the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign and the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram, she said these initiatives reinforce the spirit of patriotism, national unity and pride. She also felicitated freedom fighters’ families, war widows, gallantry award winners, sportspersons, officials, students and other achievers for their outstanding contributions. *Haryana Playing a Key Role in Strengthening India’s Economic Power- Deputy Speaker Dr. Krishan Lal Middha* Haryana Vidhan Sabha Deputy Speaker, Dr. Krishan Lal Middha, addressing the 80th Independence Day function at Gurugram after hoisting the national flag, said Haryana is strengthening its role as a key driver of India’s economic growth and moving rapidly towards the goal of Viksit Haryana alongside Viksit Bharat. He said Haryana’s GSDP is estimated at around Rs. 15.18 lakh crore in 2026-27, registering nearly 11 per cent growth over the previous year. The Government is focusing on industry, agriculture, services, investment, infrastructure and employment while ensuring that the benefits of development reach every section of society. Dr Krishan Lal Middha said the State is empowering the four key pillars of Viksit Bharat—youth, farmers, women and the poor. Around 425 dependents of martyrs have been provided government jobs on compassionate grounds over the past nearly 12 years, reflecting the State’s commitment to the families of its brave soldiers. Highlighting this year’s Independence Day theme, ‘Yuva Shakti—Leading the Journey of Viksit Bharat 2047’, he said Haryana is providing youth opportunities in education, skills, employment, sports and self-employment while working to keep them away from drugs. He also said the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram is an occasion to draw inspiration from the freedom struggle and strengthen national unity and progress. *Eight Decades of Democracy Have Made India a Strong, Empowered and Democratic Nation- Minister of State Rajesh Nagar* Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister Sh. Rajesh Nagar, addressing the 80th Independence Day function at Rewari after hoisting the national flag, said eight decades of India’s democratic journey have established the country as a strong, empowered and vibrant democracy. He said India is moving rapidly towards self-reliance, innovation and economic growth under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, to build a Viksit Bharat. He stressed the importance of youth participation and highlighted the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram as a symbol of India’s freedom consciousness and patriotism. Sh. Rajesh Nagar said Haryana is committed to the welfare of martyrs’ families, with around 425 dependents of martyrs provided government jobs on compassionate grounds over the past nearly 12 years. He said the Shaheedi Smarak being constructed at Ambala Cantonment is nearing completion and will preserve the legacy of Haryana’s brave freedom fighters. He also called for a drug-free Haryana, saying the State will intensify awareness efforts under the nationwide ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ campaign by involving youth, educational institutions, social organisations and all sections of society. *Viksit Haryana by 2047 with Prosperous Farmers, Self-Reliant Youth and Empowered Daughters is Our Resolve-Sports Minister Gaurav Gautam* Minister of State for Sports, Youth Empowerment and Entrepreneurship and Law & Legislative Affairs, Sh. Gaurav Gautam, addressing the 80th Independence Day function at Palwal after hoisting the national flag, called upon the youth to actively contribute to nation-building and strengthen the unity and integrity of the country. He said the State Government’s goal is to build a Viksit Haryana in line with Prime Minister, Sh. Narendra Modi’s vision of a Viksit Bharat. By 2047, India should be developed, self-reliant and a leading global nation, while Haryana should emerge among the country’s most developed states. He envisioned a Haryana where farmers are prosperous, youth are self-reliant, daughters are safe and empowered, poor families lead dignified lives, and villages and cities develop equally. Highlighting Palwal’s development, Sh. Gaurav Gautam said Shri Vishwakarma Skill University at Dudhola is creating new opportunities for skill development, employment and self-employment. The elevated road has improved traffic movement, while work is progressing on beautification, roads, sports facilities and other infrastructure. He said efforts would be made to develop an international-level sports stadium in Palwal, while the proposed medical college at Pelak would strengthen healthcare services. He also expressed hope that Palwal would get the Metro facility in the coming period. He said Haryana’s sportspersons have brought laurels to the State and the country at national and international levels, and the Government is continuously strengthening sports infrastructure, training and opportunities. Schemes such as Super-100 and Government Model Sanskriti Schools are providing quality education and better opportunities to government-school students, enabling them to reach IITs, NITs and premier medical institutions. The Minister said the Government is focusing on industry, MSMEs, employment and self-employment, with farmers, youth, women and the poor at the centre of development. Haryana is ensuring MSP procurement of 24 crops, while schemes including Lado Lakshmi are aimed at women’s empowerment. He also stressed the resolve for a drug-free Haryana and urged youth to stay away from drugs and channel their energy towards sports, education, skills and employment.Sh. Gaurav Gautam paid floral tributes at the Shaheed Smarak and saluted the sacrifices of freedom fighters and martyrs. He said the Shaheedi Smarak being constructed at Ambala will inspire future generations. He also highlighted Haryana’s role in the 1857 uprising, recalling the spark of freedom that emerged from Ambala.
